system.name: MMCL (tabular-imaging contrastive framework; label-as-a-feature variant LaaF)
system.one_liner: A self-supervised contrastive framework that pairs images with tabular records to pretrain unimodal encoders, plus a label-as-a-feature variant for supervised contrastive learning.

content.variant_note: graphical-abstract style: three numbered columns, one per contribution, each a small encoder-projector-embedding pipeline that ends in a latent-space sketch
content.argues: One contrastive framework can pair images with tabular records; the figure shows a morphometric feature or the label shaping the shared latent space, which the caption says boosts downstream performance.
content.subject: Three columns of image-plus-table contrastive pipelines: full clinical table, one morphometric feature, the label, each ending in a shaded latent space

lessons.what_to_learn: Run one minimal pipeline once per contribution and change a single input at a time, then repaint the changed input's colours onto the latent-space blob to show its effect; keep one colour per sample from input to embedding.
lessons.suits: A base method plus a few findings or variants that alter one input or loss term and reorganise the learned embedding space, such as contrastive or multimodal pretraining.

evidence: We combine imaging and tabular data in a contrastive learning framework.
morphometric features, describing shape and size, are of outsized importance in multimodal contrastive training
By simply adding the label as a tabular feature we introduce a novel form of supervised contrastive learning

summary: The paper proposes a self-supervised contrastive framework that pretrains image and tabular encoders on cardiac MR slices paired with clinical tables, combining SimCLR and SCARF. Figure 1 is three numbered columns divided by dashed lines. Column 1 draws the full framework: a stack of MR slices through a slab-stack image encoder and projector, a clinical table through a small node-link MLP, and coloured embeddings (circles for images, squares for tables) placed in a kidney-shaped latent space with red and green arrows labelled CLIP Loss. Columns 2 and 3 repeat a minimal pipeline with a single table column, ventricle volume or the infarction label, and paint the latent space by that feature (a gradient, or red and green patches). One colour per subject, S1 to S3, runs through the whole figure.
summary_zh: 论文提出用心脏 MR 图像与临床表格做自监督对比学习。图分三列：第一列画完整框架，图像和表格各经编码器、投影头得到嵌入，在潜空间用 CLIP 损失比较；二、三列只换表格输入（心室容积、标签），潜空间随之着色。
notes: Primary kind changed from the prior side-by-side-contrast to contribution-mosaic (paper-roadmap): the three numbered columns are the paper's three contributions (framework, morphometric finding, label as a feature), not competing designs; columns 2 and 3 do vary one input at a time, so side-by-side-contrast stays as a secondary kind. System name taken from the repository URL (MMCL) and the abstract (LaaF). The red versus green arrows are read as different-subject versus same-subject pairs of the CLIP loss from their colour logic (green joins the teal pair) and from the label; the figure has no legend for them. The digest counts three bitmaps of about 100 x 103 pt, probably the three latent-space blobs; the nine small placements are the MR slices. Image encoder drawn as layer-stack; the table encoder is a network glyph.
